yak-doglyadaty-za-granitnoyu-stilnytseyu.title: How to care for a granite countertop: rules and mistakes
yak-doglyadaty-za-granitnoyu-stilnytseyu.h1: Caring for a granite countertop — step-by-step rules
yak-doglyadaty-za-granitnoyu-stilnytseyu.description: Caring for a granite countertop: daily cleaning, safe products, sealing, removing oil and wine stains, common mistakes.
yak-doglyadaty-za-granitnoyu-stilnytseyu.dek: A daily routine without acids, abrasives or random chemicals.
yak-doglyadaty-za-granitnoyu-stilnytseyu.intro: A granite countertop does not need special care, but it does need the right care. Most problems people bring to us result from one of three things: aggressive chemicals, forgotten sealing, or an attempt to scrub a stain with an abrasive. Here is the short set of rules we hand to clients together with the countertop.

sections.heading: How to clean granite daily?
sections.body:
Warm water, a soft cloth or sponge, a few drops of neutral detergent. Wipe, rinse with clean water, dry off so no streaks remain on dark stone. That is the whole daily routine.

Wipe up spills immediately, especially oil, wine, coffee and beetroot. Sealed granite will not absorb them in a minute, but overnight under a puddle of oil a shadow may remain. Do not leave wet bags or rusty tins on the surface: rust penetrates the pores.

sections.heading: Which products are allowed and which are forbidden?
sections.body:
Allowed: products labelled “for natural stone” or “pH-neutral”, ordinary washing-up liquid in a small amount, isopropyl alcohol for degreasing before sealing.

Forbidden: vinegar, citric acid, limescale removers, chlorine and oven cleaners, abrasive powders, melamine sponges, metal scrapers. Acids and alkalis destroy the sealant and dull the polish over time; abrasives leave scratches visible against the light.

sections.heading: Is sealing needed and how often?
sections.body:
Yes. The sealant (impregnator) fills the micropores and stops liquids from penetrating. We apply it after installation; after that the owner renews it themselves.

The frequency is set by the water test, not the calendar. Pour a tablespoon of water on the work area by the sink and wait 15 minutes. If the stone under the water has darkened, it is time to renew the sealant. For polished granite that is usually every one to three years, for honed more often.

Procedure: clean and dry the surface, apply the impregnator with a sponge in a thin layer, wait as instructed (usually 10–20 minutes), wipe off the excess dry. Excess that dries on the surface leaves marks, so wipe thoroughly.

sections.heading: What to do with an oil or wine stain?
sections.body:
Fresh stain: blot with a paper towel without rubbing and wash with a neutral cleaner. In most cases that is enough.

Old grease stain: make a paste of baking soda and water to the consistency of sour cream, apply a 5 mm layer over the stain, cover with film and leave for 12–24 hours. The paste draws the oil out of the pores. Remove, rinse, repeat if needed.

Organic stain (wine, coffee, juice): the same paste, but with 3 % hydrogen peroxide instead of water. On dark granite test first on an inconspicuous spot. Rust and unknown stains are best shown to us: an overall photo and a close-up are enough for advice.

sections.heading: What should you never do?
sections.body:
Do not cut on the stone without a board: the granite will not suffer, but the knives will be blunt within a week. Do not stand on the counter or sit on the overhang: the slab is designed for distributed load, not a point load of 80 kg on the edge.

Do not put a hot frying pan on the joint between slabs or at the cut-out by the hob: local overheating of the glued joint can weaken it. Granite itself is not afraid of heat. Do not use waxes or household “polishes”: they leave a sticky film that collects dirt and has nothing to do with stone polishing.

rows: Soft cloth, neutral cleaner, wipe dry
Dull the polish, destroy the sealant
Avoid only joints and cut-out edges
Frequency set by the water test
Do not rub with an abrasive

faq.question: Can I cut on granite?
faq.answer: The stone will not suffer from a knife, but the knife will quickly go blunt. Use a board, it is easier on both.

faq.question: Can I put hot things on it?
faq.answer: Yes, granite takes cookware from the hob and oven. The only place to put a trivet is the glued joint between slabs.

faq.question: How to remove grease?
faq.answer: Fresh — with washing-up liquid. Old — with a paste of baking soda and water for a day under film. Alkaline kitchen degreasers should not be used.

faq.question: How to bring back the shine?
faq.answer: If the surface has dulled from waxy or acidic products, first wash it with a neutral cleaner and alcohol. If the polish is really damaged, a craftsman restores it on site with a machine and diamond pastes.

dogljad-za-marmurom-vanna.title: Marble care: how to clean and remove stains
dogljad-za-marmurom-vanna.h1: How to care for marble and remove stains
dogljad-za-marmurom-vanna.description: Marble care: safe products, what destroys the stone, how to remove organic, grease and rust stains, how often to seal.
dogljad-za-marmurom-vanna.dek: Safe care for a calcite surface without acids.
dogljad-za-marmurom-vanna.intro: Marble consists of calcite, and calcite dissolves in acids. That is the only thing to remember, and all care follows from it: no acidic products, quick wiping, regular sealing. The rest is no harder than caring for any other surface.

sections.heading: How to clean marble safely?
sections.body:
Daily: warm water and a soft cloth. Weekly: a neutral stone cleaner diluted as instructed, then clean water and a dry cloth. On polished marble it is important to wipe dry, otherwise drop marks remain after drying, especially on dark varieties.

For the bathroom keep a separate bottle of stone cleaner and do not use on the top what you wash the toilet or tap with. Most sanitary cleaners contain acid against limescale.

sections.heading: Which products destroy marble?
sections.body:
Acids: vinegar, lemon, descalers and limescale removers, some glass and tile cleaners. They do not stain but etch: within minutes a matte drop-shaped spot appears on a polished surface.

Alkalis and chlorine: bleaches and oven cleaners eat away the sealant and discolour coloured marble. Abrasives: powders, melamine sponges, stiff brushes scratch calcite, which is softer than sand.

Cosmetics: body oils, hair dye, some alcohol-based perfumes with dyes. Put bottles on a tray and wipe drops immediately.

sections.heading: How to remove organic, grease and rust stains?
sections.body:
First identify the type. A matte colourless spot is acid etching; it is not washed but polished. A coloured stain in the pores is dirt that is drawn out with a poultice.

Organic (coffee, tea, wine, cosmetics): a paste of white paper towel or starch moistened with 3 % hydrogen peroxide, under film for 12–24 hours. Grease (oil, cream): a paste of baking soda and water, the same time. Rust: only special acid-free marble pastes; household rust removers contain acid and will ruin the stone.

After the poultice the surface is rinsed, dried and the treatment repeated if needed. Always renew the sealant after removing a stain.

sections.heading: How often to seal marble?
sections.body:
In the bathroom once a year for the top and floor, once every two years for walls. On a kitchen window sill or table — once a year. The test is the same as for granite: a drop of water, 10 minutes, a dark spot means it is time.

It is important to understand that sealing protects against stains but not against acids. A honed finish also helps against etching: acid marks are almost invisible on it, and for a busy bathroom we recommend exactly that.

rows: Test first on an inconspicuous spot
Do not rub, give the poultice time
Cannot be washed off, it is a surface change

faq.question: Can I use vinegar or lemon?
faq.answer: No. Both etch calcite within minutes. Deposits on marble are removed with neutral stone cleaners or a mild baking soda paste.

faq.question: How to remove coffee or wine?
faq.answer: Fresh — with water and a cloth. What has soaked in — with a 3 % hydrogen peroxide poultice for 12–24 hours under film.

faq.question: How to bring back the shine?
faq.answer: Household “polishes” will not help. A surface dulled by acids is restored by a craftsman: grinding, polishing and new sealing on site within a few hours.

faq.question: Is an annual treatment needed?
faq.answer: Yes, sealing once a year for tops and floors in wet zones. It is 20 minutes of work with a sponge and the cheapest way to extend the life of marble.

pidvikonnya-z-kamenyu-marmur-granit.title: Stone window sill: marble or granite?
pidvikonnya-z-kamenyu-marmur-granit.h1: A stone window sill — marble or granite?
pidvikonnya-z-kamenyu-marmur-granit.description: Stone window sill: marble or granite, thickness, overhang, installation and care. What to choose for a sunny side, plants and moisture.
pidvikonnya-z-kamenyu-marmur-granit.dek: Choosing the stone for sun, moisture, plants and daily use.
pidvikonnya-z-kamenyu-marmur-granit.intro: A window sill is the simplest way to bring natural stone into a home: one slab, one day of installation and decades without replacement. The only question is the stone. Granite takes plant pots, water and sun without reminders about care; marble looks softer and warmer but asks for attention. We explain how we choose.

sections.heading: What to choose for a window sill?
sections.body:
For the kitchen, children's room and sills with plants choose granite: Grey Ukraine, Kometa Black, or quartz if you need a light uniform colour. For the bedroom, living room and bathroom, where the sill works as a shelf rather than a work surface, Crema Marfil or Bianco Carrara marble is appropriate.

If the windows face south and dark objects will stand on the sill, consider heating: dark granite gets hot in the sun, light marble and quartz stay cool. Do not, however, place quartz in direct sun all day: the resin can change shade over the years.

sections.heading: Why is granite better than marble for a sill?
sections.body:
Granite is not afraid of water from under pots, acid from fertilisers, cup marks or a cat's claws. The sealant is renewed every few years, not every year. It is harder, so the edge does not chip from a knock by the window frame or a mop during cleaning.

Marble wins elsewhere: it is more pleasant to touch, gives a light warm tone that granite cannot, and looks right in classic interiors. If the pots stand on saucers and the sill is not flooded, marble lasts just as long.

sections.heading: What are the advantages of stone over plastic and wood?
sections.body:
Stone does not yellow, does not warp from the radiator below and the sun above, does not absorb smells and does not scratch the way PVC does. It is heavier, and that is its advantage: the slab lies on mortar and does not “play”, and a deep 400–600 mm sill holds a person who sits on it with a book.

Wood is beautiful but needs varnish and fears water under pots. Stone is installed once and usually for the whole life of the window, and when the window is replaced the slab is reset.

sections.heading: How are fabrication and installation done?
sections.body:
Measurement after the window is installed and the reveals plastered: we record the length, depth, overhang, edge shape and whether the slab goes into the reveals. The standard overhang is 30–50 mm from the wall, thickness 20 mm; for deep sills over 500 mm or lengths over 2 m we take 30 mm.

Installation: the slab is laid on cement mortar or installation foam on a levelled base with a slight slope towards the room, no more than 1–2 mm, so water from the window does not collect by the frame. A 3–5 mm gap is left between the slab and the frame for sealant, and pads are placed under the slab so as not to disturb the radiator's ventilation. The work takes a day; the sill can be used the next day.

faq.question: Which lasts longer?
faq.answer: Granite: it is harder and does not react to acids. Marble lasts just as long if it is sealed and not flooded.

faq.question: Is it afraid of sun or moisture?
faq.answer: Granite and marble are not afraid of sun. Quartz in direct sun all day can change shade over the years. None of the stones fears moisture; only dirt in the pores does harm.

faq.question: What thickness?
faq.answer: Standard 20 mm. For long sills over 2 m, deep ones over 500 mm or with a large overhang we take 30 mm.

faq.question: Is a non-standard shape possible?
faq.answer: Yes: rounded corners, cut-outs for reveals, a bay window sill from several slabs, a sill-countertop that flows into the kitchen work area.

shody-z-granitu-cina-vygotovlennya.title: Granite stairs: fabrication, finishing, cost
shody-z-granitu-cina-vygotovlennya.h1: Granite stairs — how they are chosen and made
shody-z-granitu-cina-vygotovlennya.description: Granite stairs: overlay and solid, finish for exteriors and interiors, slip resistance, step dimensions and what makes up the cost.
shody-z-granitu-cina-vygotovlennya.dek: Structure, finish and a safe detail for interiors and exteriors.
shody-z-granitu-cina-vygotovlennya.intro: Granite stairs are the most durable part of a house: porches of Ukrainian granite stand for 50 years without repair. But it is on stairs that mistakes cost the most, because a slippery step or undrained water is felt every day. We explain how we design stairs for houses, entrance halls and shops.

sections.heading: What kinds of granite stairs are there?
sections.body:
By structure: overlay (treads and risers from 20–30 mm slabs on a concrete base) and solid (massive 100–150 mm blocks that are the steps themselves). Overlay stairs are used in 90 % of cases, both in houses and outdoors.

By location: interior (polished or honed finish, wooden or stone risers, a skirting along the wall) and exterior (flamed finish, a slope for water, a drip edge under the tread, frost-resistant adhesive).

sections.heading: Overlay or solid — what is the difference?
sections.body:
Overlay stairs are lighter, cheaper and allow any finish. A 30 mm tread with a drip edge and a 20 mm riser are laid on a concrete flight with stone adhesive. They are used for straight, winding and spiral flights.

Solid blocks suit landscaping and massive entrances: retaining steps in a garden, a porch in the “stone from the quarry” style. They do not need a concrete base in the classic sense, but they need heavy machinery for installation and cost significantly more because of the volume of material.

sections.heading: What finish is needed for outdoors?
sections.body:
For exterior stairs polishing is dangerous: in rain and frost it turns into an ice rink. We use flaming (the surface is torched, the crystals flake and give a rough texture) or bush-hammering (mechanical pitting). Both finishes are slip-resistant even when wet.

A compromise for interiors where you want shine: a polished tread with flamed or sandblasted strips 30–40 mm wide near the edge. They work like anti-slip tape without spoiling the look. Outdoors the tread also needs a 1–2 % slope away from the building and a drip edge underneath, so water does not run onto the riser and freeze in the joint.

sections.heading: What does the cost depend on?
sections.body:
Material: Ukrainian Grey Ukraine granite is more affordable than gabbro and labradorite; imports cost even more. Thickness: a 30 mm tread versus 20 mm; solid blocks separately.

Geometry: straight steps of standard 300–330 mm width are cheaper than winders and curved ones; every cut-out for a handrail or non-standard angle adds work. Finish: polishing is basic; flaming and bush-hammering cost more. Plus delivery and installation, which on stairs takes longer than on a countertop, because every part is fitted on site.

A guide price for your flight is available in the calculator; the exact estimate follows measurement of the concrete base.

rows: Less slippery, easier to care for

faq.question: Are granite stairs slippery?
faq.answer: Polished — yes, especially wet. Flamed and bush-hammered — no, they are slip-resistant even in rain and frost. For interiors you can combine shine with anti-slip strips.

faq.question: What is the maximum step length?
faq.answer: From a 30 mm slab we make solid treads up to 3 m; the limit is the slab size. Longer steps are assembled from two slabs with a joint in the middle or over a support.

faq.question: What to choose for a porch?
faq.answer: Flamed Grey Ukraine or Kometa Black 30 mm thick with a drip edge. It is the most common and most reliable solution for the Ukrainian climate.

faq.question: How much does it cost?
faq.answer: It depends on the stone, thickness, number and shape of steps, finish and installation. Enter the dimensions in the calculator for a guide; we give the exact figure after measurement.

fasad-z-kamenyu-yakyy-kamin.title: Stone facade: which stone to choose for cladding
fasad-z-kamenyu-yakyy-kamin.h1: Cladding a facade in stone — which stone to choose
fasad-z-kamenyu-yakyy-kamin.description: Stone facade: granite, travertine, quartzite or porcelain. Slab thickness, ventilated facade and mechanical fixing, joints, care.
fasad-z-kamenyu-yakyy-kamin.dek: Material, subsystem, joints and water in a durable facade.
fasad-z-kamenyu-yakyy-kamin.intro: A stone facade is not “tiles glued to a wall” but an engineered system: subframe, anchors, slabs, joints and drainage. The material matters, but it is not the only thing. We explain which stone we recommend for the Ukrainian winter, how it is fixed and why granite almost always wins.

sections.heading: Which stone is best for a facade?
sections.body:
For a private house and a commercial building in our climate it is granite: it is frost-resistant (withstands over 300 freeze cycles), does not absorb water and does not fade. Travertine and sandstone are beautiful but porous and need protection and regular care. Marble on a facade quickly loses its polish from acidic city rain.

The alternative to stone is large-format Laminam or Neolith porcelain: thin, light, UV-stable, in stone or concrete decors. It works well on ventilated facades where weight matters.

sections.heading: Why is granite the practical choice?
sections.body:
Granite needs no sealing on a facade: water runs off it and dirt is washed away by rain. A flamed surface hides small batch differences and gives no glare. Ukrainian granite is available in large batches from one block, so the colour across the whole facade is uniform.

Another advantage is repairability: a damaged slab on mechanical fixing is replaced in an hour without dismantling its neighbours. For a plinth granite has no alternative at all: salt, splashes, the caretaker's shovel and knocks leave no trace on it.

sections.heading: How are facade slabs fixed?
sections.body:
The wet method (adhesive to the wall) is acceptable for plinths and small areas up to 3 m high with 20 mm slabs. Above that the facade is made ventilated: brackets and rails are fixed to the wall, and in them clamps or pins hold 30 mm slabs in kerfs on the edges.

A 4–6 mm joint is left between slabs for thermal movement, and behind the slabs a 30–50 mm ventilation gap and insulation. This way the wall does not get wet, condensation is carried away and the stone does not crack from frost. The subsystem is calculated by a structural engineer; we make the slabs with kerfs for the specific fixing.

sections.heading: Does a stone facade need care?
sections.body:
Granite: pressure washing every few years, checking the joints and fixings. No sealing is needed. Travertine and limestone: a water repellent every 3–5 years, otherwise the pores collect dirt and moss on the north side.

A plinth of any stone should be washed of salt once a year after winter. Porcelain needs nothing but washing. If the facade is done correctly, care comes down to rinsing, and the structure itself outlives the building.

faq.question: Which stone for a harsh climate?
faq.answer: Granite with a flamed finish on a ventilated facade. It is not afraid of frost, water or salt and needs no sealing.

faq.question: What slab thickness?
faq.answer: 20 mm for adhesive fixing on a plinth, 30 mm for a ventilated facade on clamps. Porcelain 6–12 mm on its own subsystem.

faq.question: Does granite fade?
faq.answer: No. Granite's minerals are stable to ultraviolet; the colour after 30 years is the same. Only the polish can change, which is why a honed or flamed finish is used on facades.

faq.question: How to care for it?
faq.answer: Pressure washing every few years and an inspection of the joints. For porous stones additionally a water repellent every 3–5 years.

granitna-chy-vibropresovana-brukivka.title: Granite or vibro-pressed paving: which is better
granitna-chy-vibropresovana-brukivka.h1: Granite or vibro-pressed paving — what to choose
granitna-chy-vibropresovana-brukivka.description: Granite or vibro-pressed paving: strength, durability, look, repair and life-cycle cost. What to choose for a yard, paths and a driveway.
granitna-chy-vibropresovana-brukivka.dek: Paving material for a yard, paths and a car driveway.
granitna-chy-vibropresovana-brukivka.intro: Vibro-pressed concrete paving is cheaper at the start; granite paving is cheaper after 20 years. That is the main thesis, and the rest of the article explains why and in which cases concrete is still justified. We make granite paving from Ukrainian stone and see both materials on sites every day.

sections.heading: What to choose for a yard?
sections.body:
For a driveway, access road and parking space choose granite: split or sawn-split setts 100 × 100 × 50–100 mm withstand the weight of a car and a salty winter without change. For garden paths where only people walk, both materials suit, and here budget and look decide.

If the yard is large, a common compromise is granite on the driveway, entrance and along the facade, concrete in the utility zone. That way the most visible areas get a material for the whole life of the house.

sections.heading: Why is granite paving stronger?
sections.body:
Granite is a monolithic natural stone with a compressive strength of 180–220 MPa. Concrete paving has a strength of 40–60 MPa and consists of cement stone with aggregate. Under wheels and in frost concrete crumbles at the edges over time and loses its pigmented top layer; granite does not change.

Granite's water absorption is below 0.2 %, so water does not penetrate the stone and does not break it when freezing. In concrete it is 4–6 %. After 10–15 winters the difference is visible to the naked eye: granite paving looks freshly laid, concrete needs replacing.

sections.heading: When is vibro-pressed paving justified?
sections.body:
When the budget is limited and the plot is large without heavy traffic. When exact repeatable geometry and colour are needed for a geometric pattern. When the surface is temporary or the yard is to be re-planned in a few years.

Quality concrete from a large manufacturer, 60–80 mm thick and on a correct base, lasts 10–15 years and looks neat. The problems start with cheap paving from dubious plants: it loses colour in two seasons and flakes.

sections.heading: What about the cost per square metre?
sections.body:
Material: granite paving is several times more expensive than concrete. Laying: roughly the same for both, because the base and the work are the same. Life cycle: granite is laid once, concrete is relaid every 10–15 years together with the work and removal of the old.

There is also an indirect saving: granite paving lifted for, say, utility repairs is laid back, while concrete is usually thrown away. A guide for your area can be calculated in the paving calculator.

faq.question: Which lasts longer?
faq.answer: Granite: its service life is measured in decades without a change in appearance. Concrete paving is designed for 10–15 years in our climate.

faq.question: Which is cheaper?
faq.answer: At the start — concrete. Over the life cycle with relaying — granite, because it is laid once.

faq.question: What for a car driveway?
faq.answer: Granite paving 80–100 mm on a crushed-stone base. Concrete takes passenger cars, but the edges quickly crumble from manoeuvring.

faq.question: What for footpaths?
faq.answer: Both materials. Granite 50–60 mm or concrete 60 mm on a sand-and-gravel base; the choice is by look and budget.
